```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(incidenceinflation)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
```

This vignette fits the model to reports of both cases and deaths. Each
report gives, for every onset day, the cases recorded so far and how many
of them are shown as dead. The model adds to the model of cases:

- a case fatality ratio (CFR), the probability that a case dies, which can
  change at unknown onset days;
- a delay from death to the death being recorded, after a time from onset
  to death;
- a fraction of fatal cases which are recorded for their day of death
  rather than their day of onset.

We simulate an outbreak in which the CFR falls, fit the model to its
reports, and compare the estimates with the truth.

## Simulating an outbreak

The true cases arise by renewal, with $R_t$ falling from 1.2 to 0.9 on day
30. The CFR falls from 0.5 to 0.3 on the same day. Cases are reported after
a gamma delay (mean 7, sd 4 days). A fatal case dies a gamma time after
onset (mean 9, sd 5 days), and its death is recorded a further gamma delay
later (mean 4, sd 3 days). A quarter of fatal cases are recorded for their
day of death. A report is made every third day.

```{r simulate}
set.seed(1)
n_days <- 60
serial <- list(mean = 5, sd = 3)
Rt <- function(t) ifelse(t < 30, 1.2, 0.9)
# 40 days before the first onset day give the renewal its history
cases_all <- true_cases(n_days + 40, function(t) Rt(t - 40), kappa = 1000, serial,
                        initial_parameters = list(mean = 4, length = 10))
cases_before <- cases_all[1:40]
cfr <- ifelse(seq_len(n_days) < 30, 0.5, 0.3)
sim <- simulate_cases_deaths(
  cases_all[41:(n_days + 40)],
  report_days = seq(3, n_days, by = 3),
  reporting_parameters = list(mean = 7, sd = 4),
  cfr = cfr,
  death_parameters = list(mean = 4, sd = 3),
  onset_to_death = list(mean = 9, sd = 5),
  dated_by_death = list(fraction = 0.25))
snapshots <- sim$snapshots
head(snapshots)
```

`sim$truth` holds, for each onset day, the true cases and fatal cases
recorded for it (`cases_true`, `deaths_true`), the CFR and how many of the
fatal cases are dated by death.

The counts of an onset day grow from report to report. Here are the cases
and deaths of every onset day in four of the reports, against the final
truth:

```{r reports, fig.height = 5}
shown <- c(15, 30, 45, 60)
snapshots %>%
  filter(time_reported %in% shown) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(cases_reported, deaths_reported), names_to = "series", values_to = "count") %>%
  mutate(series = ifelse(series == "cases_reported", "Cases", "Deaths")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(time_onset, count)) +
  geom_line(data = sim$truth %>%
              pivot_longer(c(cases_true, deaths_true), names_to = "series", values_to = "count") %>%
              mutate(series = ifelse(series == "cases_true", "Cases", "Deaths")),
            colour = "black") +
  geom_line(aes(colour = factor(time_reported))) +
  facet_wrap(~series, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  scale_colour_viridis_d(end = 0.85, name = "Report on day") +
  labs(x = "Onset day", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()
```

The recent onset days of each report are far from complete, for deaths
even more than for cases.

## Fitting the model

`mcmc_single()` runs one chain. The cases enter as for the model of cases
alone; the deaths enter through its `deaths` argument, a list of the
reported deaths (`snapshot`) and the `settings` of the model of deaths (see
`deaths_settings()`). Here those settings give:

- `initial_cfr`: the CFR to start from;
- `onset_to_death`: the time from onset to death, which is taken as known;
  the delay estimated is then that from death to the death being recorded,
  starting from `initial_delay`;
- `dated_by_death`: a uniform prior on the fraction of fatal cases recorded
  for their day of death, fitted in its exact form.

The CFR and the delay to a death being recorded can each change at unknown
onset days, as $R_t$ and the reporting delay can.

```{r fit}
largest <- snapshots %>%
  group_by(time_onset) %>%
  summarise(cases_true = max(cases_reported))
# a starting point for the true cases: the largest count reported, inflated
# for recent onset days
days_before_end <- n_days - largest$time_onset
initial_cases <- largest %>%
  mutate(cases_true = ceiling(cases_true * (1 + 2 * exp(-days_before_end / 4)) +
                                5 * (days_before_end < 5)))

niterations <- 400
fit <- mcmc_single(
  niterations = niterations,
  snapshot_with_Rt_index_df = snapshots %>%
    select(time_onset, time_reported, cases_reported) %>%
    mutate(Rt_index = 1),
  priors = list(
    Rt = list(shape = 1, rate = 1),
    reporting = list(mean_mu = 7, mean_sigma = 10, sd_mu = 5, sd_sigma = 5),
    max_cases = ceiling(4 * max(initial_cases$cases_true) + 50),
    Rt_changepoints = list(),
    reporting_changepoints = list(min_length = 14, n_partition_moves = 20)),
  serial_parameters = serial,
  initial_cases_true = initial_cases,
  initial_reporting_parameters = list(mean = 7, sd = 4),
  initial_Rt = tibble(Rt_index = 1, Rt = 1),
  cases_before = cases_before,
  print_to_screen = FALSE,
  deaths = list(
    snapshot = snapshots %>% select(time_onset, time_reported, deaths_reported),
    settings = list(
      initial_cfr = 0.4,
      onset_to_death = list(mean = 9, sd = 5),
      dated_by_death = list(fraction = list(alpha = 1, beta = 1, initial = 0.25),
                            exact = TRUE),
      initial_delay = list(mean = 4, sd = 3))))
```

The result is a list of tables of draws, each with a column `iteration`.
Among them:

- `fit$cases`: the true cases of each onset day (`cases_true`);
- `fit$Rt`: $R_t$ of each onset day;
- `fit$deaths`: for each onset day, the true fatal cases (`deaths_true`),
  the CFR (`cfr`) and the delay to a death being recorded;
- `fit$deaths_parameters`: for each iteration, the number of changes in the
  CFR (`n_cfr_changes`) and the fraction dated by death (`dated_fraction`),
  among others.

This short chain of `r niterations` iterations takes a few minutes. We
keep its second half and summarise the draws for each onset day by their
median and 90% interval:

```{r summarise}
kept <- function(df) filter(df, iteration > niterations / 2)
by_day <- function(df, column) df %>%
  kept() %>%
  group_by(time_onset) %>%
  summarise(median = median(.data[[column]]), lower = quantile(.data[[column]], 0.05),
            upper = quantile(.data[[column]], 0.95), .groups = "drop")
results <- list(cfr = by_day(fit$deaths, "cfr"), Rt = by_day(fit$Rt, "Rt"),
                cases = by_day(fit$cases, "cases_true"),
                deaths = by_day(fit$deaths, "deaths_true"),
                parameters = kept(fit$deaths_parameters))
```

A chain this short is enough to show what the model does, but not for
inference. For that, run several chains from different starting values
(for example, different `initial_cfr` and `initial_delay`), each for
thousands of iterations, and check that they agree (for example with
`posterior::rhat()`).

## The estimates

The CFR and $R_t$ by onset day (median and 90% interval), against the
values used to simulate:

```{r cfr-Rt, fig.height = 5}
truth <- tibble(time_onset = seq_len(n_days), CFR = cfr, Rt = Rt(seq_len(n_days))) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(CFR, Rt), names_to = "quantity", values_to = "value")
bind_rows(mutate(results$cfr, quantity = "CFR"), mutate(results$Rt, quantity = "Rt")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(time_onset)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = median), colour = "steelblue4") +
  geom_line(data = truth, aes(y = value), linetype = "dashed") +
  facet_wrap(~quantity, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Onset day", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

The true cases and fatal cases recorded for each onset day, against the
last report (grey) and the truth (black):

```{r nowcast, fig.height = 5}
last <- snapshots %>%
  filter(time_reported == max(time_reported)) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(cases_reported, deaths_reported), names_to = "series", values_to = "count") %>%
  mutate(series = ifelse(series == "cases_reported", "Cases", "Deaths"))
truth_counts <- sim$truth %>%
  pivot_longer(c(cases_true, deaths_true), names_to = "series", values_to = "count") %>%
  mutate(series = ifelse(series == "cases_true", "Cases", "Deaths"))
bind_rows(mutate(results$cases, series = "Cases"), mutate(results$deaths, series = "Deaths")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(time_onset)) +
  geom_col(data = last, aes(y = count), fill = "grey80") +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = median), colour = "steelblue4") +
  geom_line(data = truth_counts, aes(y = count)) +
  facet_wrap(~series, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "Onset day", y = "Count") +
  theme_minimal()
```

The fraction of fatal cases recorded for their day of death (simulated:
0.25), and the number of changes in the CFR (simulated: one):

```{r parameters}
quantile(results$parameters$dated_fraction, c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95))
table(results$parameters$n_cfr_changes) / nrow(results$parameters)
```

## Other parts of the model

The model of deaths has other parts, each switched on through the
`settings` of `deaths` (see `deaths_settings()`):

- wrong records, which are later withdrawn
  (`initial_revision_parameters` of `mcmc_single()`);
- deaths which bring about the report of their case (`triggered`);
- a different reporting delay for fatal cases (`fatal_delay`);
- a backlog of deaths recorded long after they happen (`recording_backlog`).
